(p-589)

Surah "An-Naba" (The Tidings)

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿ʿAmma﴾. Its original form is "ʿan mā" (from what), and it was also read in this form. Then the nūn was assimilated into the mīm, so it became "ʿammā," and this was also read. Then the alif was deleted for lightness, due to its frequent use in interrogation, and the common usage follows this form. This is an interrogation expressing grandeur (istifhām tafkhīm) regarding that about which one asks, because (exalted is He) nothing hidden is concealed from Him.

﴿Yatasā'alūn﴾: some of them ask one another, or they ask others among the believers. The pronoun refers to the people of Makkah, who used to ask one another among themselves about the Resurrection (al-baʿth), and they would ask the believers about it, in a manner of mockery.

Translation:

﴿Concerning the great news﴾, i.e., the resurrection (al-ba'th). It is an explanation of the matter's magnitude, and its implied construction is: "About what do they ask one another? They ask one another concerning the great news."

﴿Concerning that about which they dispute﴾. Among them are those who firmly deny it, and among them are those who are in doubt. It is also said: the pronoun refers to both the Muslims and the disbelievers, and they were all asking one another about it; the Muslim asks in order to increase in awe, and the disbeliever asks in mockery.

"Nay," a rebuke against their disputing, or against their asking about it mockingly.

"They will soon know," a warning to them that they will know with certainty, by direct sight, that what they are asking about is true.

Then no! They will soon know.

The repetition of the rebuke (ar-radʿ) is for emphasis (at-tashdid), and "then" (thumma) indicates that the second is more forceful than the first and more intense.

(p-590) ﴿Have We not made the earth﴾ — when they denied the resurrection, it was said to them: Did not He who is credited with the resurrection create these wondrous creatures? So why do you deny His power to resurrect? The resurrection is nothing but an invention like these inventions. Or it was said to them: Why did He do these things? The Wise does not act in vain, and denying the resurrection leads to the conclusion that He is acting in vain in everything He has done.

﴿A cradle﴾: a bed, a spread. He spread it for you so that you could settle upon it.
﴿And the mountains as stakes﴾, for the earth, lest it sway with you.
﴿And We created you in pairs,﴾ male and female.

And We made your sleep a rest (subat), a cessation of your activities and a repose for your bodies; and "al-sabt" means cutting off.

Wait, I should translate the passage faithfully as given. Here is the corrected rendering:

And We made your sleep "subat" (a cutting-off of your activities, and a rest for your bodies). And "al-subat" (السبت) means cutting off.
﴿And We made the night a garment﴾, a covering that conceals you from eyes when you wish to hide what you would not like to be seen.
"And We made the day for livelihood" (Q. 78:11): a time for livelihood, in which you move about attending to your needs and your means of earning.

"And We have built above you seven [heavens] of strength (shidad)." (Qur'an 78:12)

Seven heavens (sab' samawat), (are meant). Shidad is the plural of shadidah, meaning firmly fashioned and strong, such that the passage of time has no effect on them; or it means thick, the thickness of each one being a five-hundred-year journey.
And We have made a blazing lamp (﴿وَجَعَلْنا سِراجًا وهّاجًا﴾), shining and burning brightly, meaning: combining light and heat. The intended referent is the sun.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 78, verse 14:

﴿And We have sent down from the squeezing clouds﴾, i.e., the clouds, when they are squeezed (uʿṣirat), meaning when the winds are about to press them so that they rain. From this comes "the girl has reached puberty (aʿṣarat al-jāriyah)", when she has come close to menstruating. Or [al-muʿṣirāt means] the winds, because they produce the clouds and milk their udders, so it is correct to make them the origin of the sending down. It has also been reported that God (Exalted is He) sends the winds, and they carry water from the sky to the clouds,

﴿water pouring forth abundantly﴾, poured out in great quantity.

"That We may bring forth thereby," — by the water —

"grain," — such as wheat and barley —

"and plants," — and herbage.

**﴿And gardens﴾**, orchards,

**﴿thickly entwined﴾**, with their trees densely intertwined. Its singular is "liff" (لِفٌّ), like "jidh'" (جِذْعٌ, trunk) with its plural "ajdha'" (أجْذاعٌ); and "lafif" (لَفِيفٌ), like "sharif" (شَرِيفٌ, noble) with its plural "ashraf" (أشْرافٌ). Or it has no singular, like "awza'" (أوْزاعٌ, groups). Or it is a plural of a plural: it is the plural of "luff" (لُفٌّ), and "al-luff" (اَللُّفُّ) is the plural of "lafa'" (لَفّاءُ), which is a tree with interlocked branches.

There is no pause (waqf) from "Alam naj'al" (أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ) to "alfafan" (أَلْفافًا), and the necessary pause (al-waqf al-darury) is on "awtadan" (أوْتادًا) and "ma'ashan" (مَعاشًا).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 78, verse 17:

﴿Indeed, the Day of Judgment is the Day of Decision﴾, between the doer of good and the doer of evil, and between the one upon the truth and the one upon falsehood.

﴿It is a appointed time﴾, a specified period and a known terminus for the occurrence of recompense, or a promised time for reward and punishment.

"The Day the Trumpet is blown" (yawma yunfakhu): a substitute (badal) for "the Day of Decision," or an explicative apposition (ʿatf bayan),

"into the Horn" (fi al-Sur): in the trumpet (al-qarn),

"and you will come forth in throngs" (fa-ta'tunna afwajan): a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: in groups of different kinds, or nations, each nation with its messenger.

﴿And the sky is opened﴾, light (*khafīf*, the reading without the doubled *tāʾ*), Kūfī (the reading of the people of Kufa), i.e., it is split, for the descent of the angels,

﴿so it becomes gates﴾, so it becomes having gates, and paths, and openings, and it has no openings today.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 78, verse 21:

﴿Indeed, Hell has been ever-lying in wait﴾. It is a path upon which the creatures pass: the believer passes over it, and the disbelievers enter it. It has been said: "al-mirsad" (the place of watching) is the boundary in which watching takes place, meaning: it is the boundary of the rebellious ones, who are kept watch over in it for punishment, and it is their return-place. Or it is a mirsad for the people of Paradise: the angels who receive them there keep watch over them, because their crossing is over it.
For the transgressors (lil-tagheen) a place of return (ma'aban), for the disbelievers a destination (marji'an).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 78, verses 23–24:

﴿Lābithīn﴾ (remaining), mākithīn (dwelling), is a qualifying circumstantial phrase (ḥāl muqaddara, a state to be realised later) from the pronoun in "lil-ṭāghīn" (for the transgressors). Ḥamzah read "labithīn" (لَبِثِينَ). "Al-labth" (اللَّبْث) is stronger, since the one who remains (lābith) is one in whom lubth (staying) has occurred, however briefly, whereas al-labth is something whose nature involves lubth and staying in a place.

﴿Fīhā﴾ (therein), in Jahannam.

﴿Aḥqāban﴾ (for ages) is an adverb of time (ẓarf). It is the plural of ḥuqub (ḥuqub, a long period of time), which means an age (dahr). It does not denote a fixed number; rather it means eternity (al-abad): whenever one ḥuqub passes, another follows it, without end. Al-ḥuqub and al-ḥuqbah are only used when the succession and continuity of times is intended. It is also said: al-ḥuqub is eighty years. Some scholars were asked about this verse, and after twenty years he answered: "Remaining therein for ages, they will not taste therein coolness or drink" – i.e., "not tasting" (ghayra dhā'iqīn), a circumstantial phrase from the pronoun of "lābithīn" – "When these ages in which they are punished by being denied coolness and drink have ended, they will be replaced by other ages in which there is another punishment; these are ages after ages, with no cessation for them."

It is also said that it derives from "ḥaqiba ʿāmunā" (our year was barren), when its rain and goodness decrease, and "ḥaqiba fulān" (so-and-so was deprived), when he failed to obtain provision; thus he is "ḥaqib," and its plural is (p-592) "aḥqāb." It then takes the accusative as a circumstantial phrase concerning them, meaning: remaining therein "ḥaqibīn" (deprived). And ﴿lā yadhūqūna fīhā bardan wa lā sharāban﴾ (they will not taste therein coolness or drink) is an explanation of it. And his statement:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 78, verse 25:

﴿Except a boiling fluid and a dark, pus-like liquid﴾. This is a disjunctive exception (istithna' munqati', an exception not of the same kind as what precedes it), meaning: they do not taste in Jahannam, or in the ages (al-ahqab), any coolness (bard), or refreshment (rawh) that would relieve them from the heat of the Fire, or sleep (nawm), and from this comes the prohibition of the coolness (man' al-bard); nor any drink that quenches their thirst. Rather, they taste in it hamim (حَمِيمًا), boiling water (ma'un harrun), which burns whatever reaches it; and ghassaq (غَسّاقًا), water that flows from their pus (sadid).

With the shadda (doubled letter), it is read by the Kufans other than Abu Bakr (ghayr Abi Bakr).

﴿Jaza'an﴾ (a recompense): they were recompensed with a recompense.

﴿Wifaqan﴾ (in accordance): corresponding to their deeds. It is a verbal noun (masdar) in the sense of an adjective, or it means "one having correspondence (wifaq)." Then he resumed, giving the reason, saying:
Qur'an 78:27: ﴿Indeed, they used not to hope for a reckoning.﴾ They did not fear God's reckoning of them, or they did not believe in the resurrection, so as to hope for a reckoning.

"And they denied Our signs with (much) denial." Kidhdhaban (كِذّابًا): tadhiban (تَكْذِيبًا), meaning denial. The pattern fi'al (فِعّالٌ), in the category of fa"ala (فَعَّلَ), is widespread throughout the whole of it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 78, verse 29:

﴿And everything﴾ is in the accusative, governed by an implied verb (fi'l mudmar) which it explains: ﴿We have enumerated it in a Book﴾, written in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh). It may be a circumstantial accusative (hal), or a verbal noun (masdar) occupying the position of "ihsa'an" (enumerating), or the phrase may be read as "ahsaynan" in the sense of "katabna" (We wrote), because enumeration (al-ihsa') generally takes place through writing. This verse is an interjection (i'tiraD), because His saying:

﴿فَذُوقُوا﴾ is a consequence (*musabbab*) of their disbelief in the Reckoning and their denial of the signs, meaning: taste your recompense. The *iltifat* (the shift in grammatical address, here from the third person to the second) is evidence of the intensity of the anger.

﴿فَلَنْ نَـزِيدَكم إلا عَذابًا﴾ [So We shall increase you only in punishment]. In a hadith: "This verse is the most severe in the Qur'an for the people of the Fire."

﴿Indeed, for the God-fearing there is a mafaz (a place of success/attainment)﴾, "maf'al", from "al-fawz" (success), which may function as a verbal noun (masdar), meaning: deliverance from every hated thing, and triumph over every beloved thing. It may also refer to a place, namely Paradise. Then he substituted for it, as a partial substitute (badal al-ba'd min al-kull), saying:

[p. 593] ﴿Gardens﴾: orchards, containing kinds of fruit-bearing trees. It is the plural of "حَدِيقَةٌ" (ḥadīqah). And "أَعْنَابًا" (aʿnāban), ﴿grapes﴾: vines. It is a coordinated noun (ʿaṭf, grammatical conjunction) upon "﴿gardens﴾".

﴿And maidens﴾ (كَواعِبَ), with swelling breasts (نَواهِدَ),

﴿of equal age﴾ (أتْرابًا): contemporaries (لِداتٌ), equal in age (مُسْتَوِياتٌ في السِنِّ).

Wa-ka'san dihaqan (﴿وَكَأْسًا دِهاقًا﴾), meaning: and a cup overflowing (filled to the brim).

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿And a cup overflowing.﴾

Commentary: "Dihaq" means full, filled.

﴿They will not hear therein﴾, in Paradise, a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring back to the pronoun in the predicate of "inna" (indeed),

﴿any idle talk (lagh'wan)﴾, meaning falsehood,

﴿nor any lying (kidhdhāban)﴾. Al-Kisa'i read it as a light form (khafīf), with the meaning of "mutual lying" (mukādhaba), i.e., that some of them do not lie to one another; or, "he does not lie to him."

Verse 36 of Surah al-Naba' (78) is quoted in its own context, so I render the passage as follows.

﴿Jazā'an﴾ (as a recompense): a verbal noun (maṣdar), meaning "He recompensed them with a recompense" (jazāhum jazā'an).

﴿Min Rabbika 'aṭā'an﴾ (from your Lord, as a gift): a verbal noun (maṣdar), or a substitute (badal) for "jazā'an".

﴿Ḥisāban﴾ (sufficient): an adjective (ṣifah), meaning "sufficient" (kāfiyan), or "in accordance with their deeds" ('alā ḥasab a'mālihim).

Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Most Merciful (﴿رَبِّ السَماواتِ والأرْضِ وما بَيْنَهُما الرَحْمَنِ﴾). With the genitive case (بِجَرِّهِما), Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim read them as a substitute (بَدَلًا) for "your Lord" (رَبِّكَ). As for the one who reads them in the nominative (رَفَعَهُما), "Lord" (رَبُّ) is the predicate of an omitted subject (خَبَرُ مُبْتَدَإٍ مَحْذُوفٍ), or it is a subject whose predicate is "the Most Merciful" (اَلرَّحْمَنُ), or "the Most Merciful" is its qualifier (صِفَتُهُ). "They do not possess" (﴿لا يَمْلِكُونَ﴾) is the predicate, or the two words are both predicates. The pronoun in "they do not possess" refers to the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, and the pronoun in "address to Him" (﴿مِنهُ خِطابًا﴾) refers to God (تَعالى), meaning: they do not possess intercession from His punishment (تَعالى), except with His permission, or no one is able to address Him (تَعالى) out of fear.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 78, verse 38:

﴿The Day when﴾, if you make it an adverbial complement (zarf) of "they will have no power" (yamlikun), then do not pause at "khitaban" (address). If you make it an adverbial complement of "they will speak" (yatakallamun), then pause.

﴿The Spirit (al-Ruh)﴾ is Jibril (Gabriel), according to the majority (al-Jumhur). It is also said: he is a great angel, and Allah (Exalted) has created nothing greater than him after the Throne (al-'Arsh).

﴿And the angels in rows (saffan)﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: arranged in rows (mustaffin).

﴿They will not speak﴾, i.e., the creatures are there, out of fear,

﴿except him whom the Most Merciful has permitted﴾ to speak, or to intercede,

﴿and he says what is right (sawaban)﴾, meaning what is true: such as when the one for whom intercession is made says, "There is no god but Allah" in the world; or it means: permission will be given only to one who speaks what is right concerning the matter of intercession.

That is the True Day (ﷺ-free): "That is the True Day" — the one whose occurrence is certain.

Let me correct and give the translation cleanly:

﴿That is the True Day﴾, the one whose occurrence is established.

﴿So whoever wills may take a return (maʾab) to his Lord﴾, a place of return, by means of righteous deeds.

﴿Indeed, We have warned you﴾, O disbelievers,

﴿of a near punishment﴾, in the Hereafter, because what is coming is near (p-594),

﴿on the Day when a man sees﴾, that is, the disbeliever, because of His saying: "Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment",

﴿what his hands have sent forward﴾, of evil, as in His saying: ﴿And taste the punishment of the burning﴾ [al-Hajj: 22] and ﴿That is for what your hands have sent forward﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 182]. The hands are singled out because most actions are done by them, even though it is possible that the hands have no part in the sins that were committed.

﴿And the disbeliever says﴾: the apparent noun is placed in the position of the pronoun to increase the reproach. Or "the man" is general, and the disbeliever is singled out from it. "What his hands have sent forward" means what he did of good and evil, or it refers to the believer, because the disbeliever is mentioned after him, and what he sent forward of good. "Mā" is interrogative, in the accusative governed by "qaddamat" (sent forward), meaning: "he sees what his hands have sent forward." Or it is relative, in the accusative governed by "yanzuru" (sees). It is said "nazartuhu," meaning "I looked at him," and the returning pronoun in the relative clause is omitted, meaning "what his hands sent forward."

﴿Oh, would that I had been dust!﴾ in the world, so that I had not been created and had not been held accountable. Or: Oh, would that I had been dust on this Day, so that I had not been resurrected. It has been said: "God gathers the animals, which are not accountable, until He takes retribution for the hornless from the horned, then He returns them to dust, so the disbeliever wishes his state were theirs." It has also been said: "The disbeliever is Iblis, who wishes to be like Adam, who was created from dust, so that he would receive the reward of Adam's believing children."
